summary:
The UnexpecTED Magazine is a 28-page digital, interactive and free magazine that explores the often-overlooked equipment and objects left behind on the Moon and Mars after NASA missions.
Space exploration is often associated with astronauts, rovers, and major discoveries. However, the stories of the equipment that made these missions possible are rarely told. We wanted to bring these forgotten stories into the spotlight.
To address this, we developed a magazine that combines scientific research, historical information, visual content, and creative storytelling. Instead of simply presenting facts, we give these objects a voice and tell their stories from their own perspectives. Our aim was to make the content easy for children to understand while also offering scientific depth and interesting details for adult readers.
We believe every object left behind has a story worth telling and a contribution worth remembering. Through our project, we hope to inspire curiosity, make space exploration accessible to different age groups, and introduce a new perspective on humanity's journey beyond Earth.
details:
The UnexpecTED Magazine is a digital science magazine designed to introduce readers to the objects and equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars after NASA missions. It takes readers through different space missions, exploring the stories of objects such as lunar modules, scientific instruments, rovers, parachutes, and heat shields.

The magazine works as a digital flipbook, allowing readers to turn its pages and explore each topic at their own pace. What makes our approach different is the way we tell these stories. Instead of presenting the objects only through technical explanations, we give them a voice and let them narrate their own journeys. This allows readers to understand not only what these objects are, but also why they were sent into space, what they accomplished, and what happened to them afterwards.

We used NASA's data, mission records, and publicly available resources as the foundation of our research to ensure that the scientific information in our magazine was reliable and accurate. We combined this research with historical context, creative storytelling, and visual content to create an engaging reading experience.

Throughout the development process, we carefully considered our target audience. We wanted a five-year-old child to be able to follow the stories while still offering enough scientific depth and interesting details to keep an adult reader engaged. For this reason, we paid particular attention to accessible language, scientific accuracy, visual selection, and the overall flow of the magazine.

Our project combines scientific research with creative writing and visual storytelling. We used NASA's resources for research, Canva to design the magazine and our presentation, and Heyzine to publish it as a digital flipbook. We did not use coding languages or specialized hardware.

Beyond introducing forgotten space equipment, we hope to change how readers look at space exploration. We want them to realize that a mission's story does not end with its landing or the completion of its objectives. Even the objects left behind have stories, purposes, and contributions worth remembering.
